_comment: Route table for the drelay relay. Every key is documented here because this file is both the
template the packaged launcher extracts and the file an operator edits by hand.
listenHost 0.0.0.0 so the relay accepts whatever address the client dials, including a claimed
server address (see upstreamHost).
upstreamHost is the LAN address the relay's own outbound dials are bound to. It is REQUIRED as
soon as a route's remoteHost is claimed locally: Windows delivers a connection to a local
address locally when the source sits on the same interface, so an unbound dial lands back in
this relay's own listener and it dials itself. Binding an address on a different interface than
the claim (the claim lives on the loopback pseudo-interface - see the bundled
Set-AddressClaim.ps1) sends the dial out to the real server. The launcher passes
-Ddrelay.upstreamHost=<the LAN address it resolved>, and refreshes the key below before each
run, so this is only a fallback when the relay is started by hand. The relay refuses to start
if a destination is claimed and this is unset, or if it names an address on the same interface
as the claim.
upstreamBindPort was only ever needed by the retired WinDivert redirect (it pinned the relay's
source port so the packet filter could exclude it). Leave it 0: Windows allows one socket per
local port, so a pinned port serializes upstream dials and fails a second concurrent session.
remoteHost must be a concrete address: a name the hosts file redirects to this machine makes
the relay dial its own listener. The launcher refreshes the addresses below from the game's own
API (Game) and DNS (Queue) on every run, so a released IP being stale is not fatal; an address
that is NOT claimed still silently bypasses the proxy - the client connects straight to the
real server.
optional marks a route whose destination may legitimately not be serving. The relay still
listens on it, so a dial the server later sends there is captured rather than bypassing the
proxy, but its closed port is reported as a note instead of a startup warning.
Game  : the live value comes from https://playdarzas.com/api/v1/serverlist -> servers[].host
(checked 2026-10-05: one server, 18.145.161.25 "Zenith").
Queue : the live address behind queue.playdarzas.com - 44.242.119.50, resolved from DNS. The
old <lan-ip> hosts entry is retired: the claim on this address captures Queue by name
resolution alone, and leaving that entry in place breaks the client whenever the relay
is not running (the name points at a dead local address).
Slave : this is the realm, and it is the one destination the client does not choose. Nothing in
the client dials port 6411 on its own; instead the server sends GmReconnect (game id 36)
mid-session naming a host and a port, and the client dials exactly that. The relay handles
that packet itself: it claims the named address on loopback and records host:port as this
port's destination BEFORE forwarding the packet on, so the client's follow-up dial is
captured and forwarded to the realm. The remoteHost below is only the fallback for a dial
that arrives before any retarget, so it is normally stale - that is expected.
logDirectory : where the per-run event log goes. Every run writes work/logs/events-<run>.jsonl
(every event), work/logs/nexus-<run>.jsonl (the escape story only, small enough to read in
full) and work/logs/relay-<run>.log. All three also go to stdout.
web : the observability dashboard, loopback only. port 0 disables it, a negative port takes any
free one, and a busy port walks forward four times. It is how a live session is watched
without reading a log: HP, the auto-nexus state and its escape acks, and a packet stream
shaped by the dashboard's own filter list (which defaults to character HP).
autoNexus : the rule that injects GmEscape when HP falls below a threshold. OFF by default, and
it starts in dry run even when switched on. Every key here is also settable as
-Ddrelay.nexus.<key> and live from the dashboard, and every change is recorded in the
event log. See docs/INJECTION.md for why this is reactive rather than a damage
predictor, and for what to check on a first live run.
strip : server->client rewrites. OFF by default, and the only setting here that changes bytes
the server sent rather than adding bytes of the relay's own. `confused` removes
StatusEffect 11 from the local player's StatsType.StatusEffects list, which is the only
channel that effect ever arrives on; the client applies it purely locally and never
expires it on a timer, so shortening the duration does nothing and removing the entry is
the only thing that works. `effect` is the ordinal to remove (11 = Confused), and
`minVotes` is how many health readings an object must match before the relay believes it
is the local player - raising it makes a mis-identification less likely and makes the
feature slower to arm. Also settable as -Ddrelay.strip.confused / .effect / .minVotes.
This is a gameplay change, not an observability one: see docs/INJECTION.md.
NOTE: the client's own copy of the list is replaced wholesale by every list the server
sends, so this must strip every occurrence, and the server will keep sending them.
